evidence: zircon_runtime/src/runtime_diagnostics/collect.rs:105-107,117-132 invokes this projection on every snapshot; zircon_runtime/src/core/runtime/diagnostics/store.rs:242-254 appends each measurement without frame-index deduplication; zircon_runtime/src/dynamic_api/session/diagnostics.rs:16 collects on request.
impact_or_question: Repeated reads of one submitted frame append duplicate history samples and change smoothing, potentially evicting distinct frames. Confirm whether the store represents sample calls or distinct rendered frames.
next_action: Decide and document sampling semantics; if history is frame based, deduplicate/replace same-frame samples and add repeated-query coverage.

evidence: zircon_runtime/src/core/framework/render/backend_types/ambient_occlusion.rs:93-98 defines artifact fingerprints as u64; ambient_occlusion.rs:38-88 passes them through usize to record_count; measurement.rs:3-15 converts usize to f64 before DiagnosticStore::record_static.
impact_or_question: Identifiers above 2^53 can round on 64-bit platforms; on 32-bit platforms u64 values above usize::MAX saturate, so the exposed fingerprint can differ from the renderer report.
next_action: Expose exact integer identity separately from numeric graph series or encode it losslessly; add a large-fingerprint contract test.

evidence: global_sdf.rs:7-69 records six *_time_us fields through record_count, and lines 177-249 record seven byte-size fields through record_count; measurement.rs:3-16 gives record_count the count unit, while record_microseconds and record_bytes use corresponding units. zircon_runtime/src/tests/runtime_diagnostics/gpu_sprite_ui_advanced.rs:233-249 asserts count for two time paths.
impact_or_question: Runtime diagnostic snapshots label Global SDF microsecond durations and byte sizes as count, so consumers relying on unit metadata misinterpret them.
next_action: Use microsecond and byte recorders for the affected fields, update snapshot unit assertions, and check u64 conversion.

evidence: graph/frame.rs:219-225 records render.taa.reactive_mask_encoded_write_bytes through record_count after casting a u64 to usize; measurement.rs:3-16 assigns count, while record_bytes at lines 19-33 assigns bytes.
impact_or_question: The TAA reactive mask upload quantity appears with count unit in runtime diagnostic snapshots even though the value is a byte size.
next_action: Use the byte recorder for this path and add a snapshot unit assertion.
